title: East Village walk
source_title: Walking Tour: East Village (Fodor's via The New York Times, 2006)

stops.name: The Strand
stops.address: 828 Broadway (at E 12th St), New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: A giant used and new bookshop where it is easy to lose an hour among the shelves. Its tote bags are a classic cheap souvenir for the rest of the walk.
stops.now: Now: still open at 828 Broadway, the shop's home since 1957.
check: Article says 'West 12th Street'; the store is actually at E 12th St, east side of Broadway.

stops.name: Grace Church
stops.address: 802 Broadway (at E 10th St), New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: A Gothic Revival Episcopal church where Broadway bends; the route turns east here onto 10th Street.
stops.now: Now: active Episcopal parish; church still stands at 802 Broadway.
stops.directions: Walk south on Broadway two blocks to E 10th St.

stops.name: Astor Place: the Alamo cube and subway kiosk
stops.address: Astor Place at 4th Ave & E 8th St, New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: Two traffic islands: one holds the big black steel cube (Tony Rosenthal's Alamo, 1967) that people push to spin; the other has the ornate cast-iron entrance to the Astor Place subway station.
stops.now: Now: the cube was removed in May 2023 for repairs and returned, spinning again, in July 2023; the subway kiosk is still in use.
stops.directions: Turn left onto E 10th St for one block, then right down 4th Ave two blocks to Astor Place.
check: No 2025-26 news found on the cube; last confirmed back and working July 2023.

stops.name: Cooper Union Foundation Building
stops.address: 7 E 7th St (Cooper Square), New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: The brownstone home of the Cooper Union college, opened in 1859; its Great Hall is where Lincoln gave a famous 1860 speech.
stops.now: Now: still Cooper Union's main building, Great Hall still used for talks and events.
stops.directions: Head east from the cube; the Foundation Building is on your right.

stops.name: St. Marks Place
stops.address: St. Marks Place (E 8th St) between 3rd & 2nd Aves, New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: The punk and counterculture strip of 8th Street, lined with tattoo, vintage and novelty shops. The article picked out three stores here: Trash and Vaudeville, Kim's Underground and the Sock Man.
stops.now: Now: none of the three is at its 2006 address. Trash and Vaudeville moved to 96 E 7th St (2016), the Sock Man moved to 99 St. Marks Pl (Nov 2016), and Kim's Video closed (2008, last store 2014).
stops.directions: Keep east across 3rd Ave onto St. Marks Place.
check: Pin is a mid-block point between 3rd and 2nd Aves, not a geocoded address.
Trash and Vaudeville at 96 E 7th St confirmed by EV Grieve, Oct 2025.
Sock Man at 99 St. Marks Pl: latest coverage found is Aug 2023 (40th anniversary); 2025-26 status unconfirmed.
Did not find what occupies 4 and 6 St. Marks Place today.

stops.name: Stuyvesant Street detour
stops.address: Stuyvesant St between 3rd Ave & E 10th St, New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: A quieter alternative to St. Marks: a diagonal old street with 1860s brick rowhouses (the Renwick Triangle) that ends at St. Mark's Church. The article sent readers past St. Mark's Bookshop on the way.
stops.now: Now: the rowhouses remain (landmark district), but St. Mark's Bookshop is gone; it left 31 Third Ave in 2014 and closed for good in Feb 2016.
stops.directions: From St. Marks Place, go one block north on 3rd Ave, then turn right onto Stuyvesant St.
check: Pin is the middle of Stuyvesant St from Nominatim.

stops.name: Original 2nd Avenue Deli site
stops.address: 156 2nd Ave (at E 10th St), New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: Corner where the famous kosher deli stood until 2006. Star-shaped plaques set in the pavement honour stars of the old Yiddish theatre that once filled Second Avenue.
stops.now: Now: a Chase bank branch occupies the corner; the deli itself moved away in 2006. The Yiddish Walk of Fame plaques were still in the sidewalk as of 2017.
stops.directions: Turn left (north) on 2nd Ave and walk two blocks to E 10th St.
check: No source after 2017 found on the plaques' condition; they were damaged and patched during curb work in Oct 2017.
Chase at 156 2nd Ave from OSM and bank directories (FDIC: branch since 2007), not from Chase's own site.
Deli's current locations (E 33rd St, 1st Ave) from memory, not re-checked this session.

stops.name: St. Mark's Church in-the-Bowery
stops.address: 131 E 10th St (at 2nd Ave), New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: Built in 1799 on Peter Stuyvesant's old farm, it is one of Manhattan's oldest churches and Stuyvesant is buried here. It has long hosted poetry and dance.
stops.now: Now: active Episcopal church, still home to the Poetry Project and Danspace Project.
stops.directions: Directly across E 10th St from the deli site. The Stuyvesant Street detour rejoins the main route here.
check: The article itself rejoins the detour at the deli (stop 6), right across the street.

stops.name: Russian & Turkish Baths
stops.address: 268 E 10th St (between 1st Ave & Ave A), New York, NY 10009
stops.summary: A bathhouse running since 1892, with steam rooms, saunas and a cold plunge pool, open to the public for a day fee.
stops.now: Now: open; it reopened in 2021 after the pandemic closure.
stops.directions: Walk east on E 10th St; the baths are just before Avenue A.
check: No 2026-specific news found; open status based on current listings. Check hours before going.

stops.name: Tompkins Square Park
stops.address: Between Aves A & B, E 7th & E 10th Sts, New York, NY 10009
stops.summary: The neighbourhood's main park, once the heart of the city's Little Germany. Today it is a mixed local hangout with a dog run and big old elms.
stops.now: Now: open city park run by NYC Parks.
stops.directions: Reach Avenue A; the park is across the avenue.
check: Pin is the park centre; the route meets it at Ave A & E 10th St.

stops.name: Avenue A
stops.address: Avenue A near E 4th St, New York, NY 10009
stops.summary: Stroll south along Avenue A, which the article remembered for old Italian bakeries and small boutiques.
stops.now: Now: still a busy strip of bars, cafes and shops.
stops.directions: Walk south on Avenue A about seven blocks toward E 3rd St.
check: Pin geocoded from 52 Avenue A (near E 4th St). Did not check which 2006 bakeries survive.

stops.name: Former Hells Angels clubhouse
stops.address: 77 E 3rd St (between 1st & 2nd Aves), New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: For 50 years the New York chapter's headquarters, famous for the row of motorcycles parked outside.
stops.now: Now: the club left in 2019 and sold the building; it was gut-renovated into apartments with a ground-floor shop, which a tattoo studio vacated in Mar 2026.
stops.directions: Turn right (west) on E 3rd St and walk past 1st Ave; No. 77 is on the north side.

stops.name: CBGB site
stops.address: 315 Bowery (at Bleecker St), New York, NY 10003
stops.summary: The tiny club where the Ramones, Blondie, Talking Heads and Patti Smith launched the New York punk scene. It closed in October 2006, the year this tour was written.
stops.now: Now: the building stands (Bowery Historic District); a John Varvatos store opened in the space in 2008, but its current tenant is unconfirmed.
stops.directions: Turn left (south) on the Bowery and walk two blocks to No. 315.
check: Varvatos store went dark in mid-2020 during the brand's bankruptcy; an undated Acadia Realty listing still names John Varvatos and Patagonia at 313-315 Bowery. Could not confirm what is there in Nov 2026.
